_about: Design decisions made from variant boards (design doc: Execution plan > Decision workflow). One record per decision, appended, never rewritten once chosen. Every record is reported to Alex so it can be added to the design doc's decision log, which stays the source of truth; this file is what the build reads.

record_shape.area: the design doc area, e.g. Trees, Shadows, Walls, UI
record_shape.question: what was being decided, in one line
record_shape.board: variants/<id>/ -- the board the choice was made from; its seed and parameter sets are in that folder's board.json
record_shape.chosen: a variant name, 'blend of A and B', or 'new round'
record_shape.status: proposed | chosen by Alex | logged in design doc

decisions.question: How transparent should cast shadows be? (Alex: shadows need to be softer, meaning more transparent)
decisions.chosen: D
decisions.notes: Alex: 'default to D for now'. Open follow-up raised with it: whether shadows should darken as the sun climbs (a sun-elevation coupling); not decided.

decisions.question: The unit art mockup's proposals: side colours, where each side's colour goes, and how far a plane's shadow sits from it
decisions.board: reference/mockups/unit_sheet.html (a mockup sheet, not a variant board)
decisions.chosen: as proposed
decisions.notes: Alex: 'I love the rest of the decisions. The accent colors are perfectly toned. Those might be useful colors to mirror in the HUD.' The pen line was left open (variants/pen-line/).

decisions.question: Should an ink line's width vary along it, and how?
options: C heavier on the shadow side
decisions.chosen: C
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Shadow side looks the best.' Factor values are the board's; tuning them is a later board.

decisions.question: The sandbox demo's baseline: map scale, turn length, steps, stalls, map edge, ready-up, empty plans, the minute of flight
decisions.board: none (a recommendation table in chat; the scale options came from Track T's and Track S's arithmetic)
decisions.chosen: as recommended

parameters.stalls: none in the demo; later a stall may cost an altitude band
parameters.map_edge: the planner refuses a step that ends outside the map; the AI turns back on its own
parameters.ready_up: editing a plan after Ready un-readies that player; the turn plays when the last player is ready
parameters.empty_plan: the plane flies on straight at its current speed
parameters.minute_of_flight: a simulated minute (about 12 turns), which sizes the map at 5,000 m

decisions.notes: Alex: '1-7 look good'. The scale is a starting value: the demo exposes it as a live knob so Alex can decide by flying. Items 8 (how height reads in ink) and 9 (terrain level fills vs object fills) are still open.

decisions.question: How does height read in ink on the full render?
decisions.chosen: B
decisions.notes: Alex: 'I strongly prefer the contours visually but I am not sure what they are signaling.' Open with it: what line breaks mean, and whether height steps are passable to ground units.

decisions.question: How do object fills relate to the ground level they stand on?
options: today: ground +0.025 L per level, fills fixed
1: fills step up with the ground
decisions.chosen: today
decisions.notes: Alex: 'For ground level fill - I actually like the current look the most.' Accepted with it: on the top level, wall and rock fills sit slightly darker than the ground (-0.018 / -0.011 L).

decisions.question: Are height steps passable to ground units, and what do the contours signal?
options: A every step a cliff, crossed at ramps or roads
B every step a slope, crossed anywhere slower
C mixed: some edges cliffs, some slopes
decisions.chosen: A

parameters.rule: every height step is a cliff: impassable to ground units, crossed only at ramps or roads
parameters.contours: tightly packed at every step (a cliff); a gap in the lines marks a ramp
parameters.contour_breaks_now: none: lines drawn unbroken until ramps exist
parameters.ramp_shadows: when ramps are added, their shadows must be complete and correct (a ramp is a sloped surface: its shadow varies along it and meets the cliff's); no partial version

decisions.notes: Alex first chose C (mixed cliffs and slopes), then: 'Actually, I take that back. Lets do A.' Also: 'draw the lines unbroken for now'. Ramps come with roads and ground units. On ramps: 'The shadows are much more complex with ramps. I don't want to do them less then 100% when we add them.'

decisions.question: Sight range, fog edge and the far-zoom view for the demo's first fog option
decisions.chosen: ~800 m sight, inked edge, overview_topo
decisions.notes: Alex: 'go with your fog recommendations'. Asked with it: show line of sight occluded, e.g. a tank's view inside a valley.

decisions.question: Unit callsigns
decisions.chosen: both lists as proposed
decisions.notes: Alex: 'add the callsigns'.

decisions.area: Fog of war, Line of sight
decisions.question: Should tree canopies block line of sight?
decisions.chosen: trees do not block, for now
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Let's disable trees blocking for now.' Line of sight itself stays off by default (vision.line_of_sight = none); terrain line of sight is a knob in the demo.

decisions.question: Should a plane's shadow gap follow the map scale or the plane's drawn size?
options: today: the gap in map metres (shrinks 4x from 4 to 1 px/m while the plane stays the same size)
proposed: the gap scaled with the plane's drawn size
decisions.chosen: proposed
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Do the proposal'. The altitude cue now reads the same at every map scale.

decisions.question: What decides what a unit's guns can hit?
options: one forward cone per plane type, plus fire at will / hold fire (proposed)
decisions.chosen: a cone per weapon

parameters.rule: every weapon has its own cone; a bomber's tail turret and its front guns are different weapons with different cones
parameters.target_priority: wanted eventually; not designed or built yet
parameters.hardpoints: every gun sits on a hardpoint, a mount point on the airframe ([forward, right, up] metres from the unit's centre); its cone starts there (Alex, later the same day: 'We will want guns to have hardpoints')

applied_to: nothing yet: the first-fight pass builds it (proposed plan in the design doc)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Let's do a cone per weapon. There's a huge difference between a turret on the back of a bomber and the front guns.' Idea Alex is still thinking through, NOT to design or build yet: a special used on an area pre-aims it, so an enemy revealed there by the fog may be hit with higher accuracy.

decisions.question: How does a weapon's fire resolve into hits?
options: no dice: damage builds inside the cone, falling off with range (proposed)
a random roll per burst from a shared seed
decisions.chosen: random-ish, from a number of factors to be modelled over time

parameters.first_factor: machine guns: better odds the closer the target is to the centre of the cone

applied_to: nothing yet: the first-fight pass builds it (proposed plan in the design doc)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'It should be randomish with a bunch of factors we will want to model later.'

decisions.question: Can guns fire between altitude bands?
options: same band, or one band away with a penalty (proposed)
decisions.chosen: the same cone behaviour in height

parameters.rule: a weapon's cone has a vertical extent too; a target above or below is in reach when it is inside the cone, with odds by the same rule as across

applied_to: nothing yet: the first-fight pass builds it (proposed plan in the design doc)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Same cone behavior.'

decisions.question: Hills cannot hide a plane (ground tops out at 24 m, the low air band is 120 m). Make the ground taller?
options: taller high ground so a low plane can drop behind a ridge (proposed)
keep the ground low; hiding is for ground units
decisions.chosen: taller ground: mountainous islands, for tactical options

parameters.deferred: off for now; revisit once there are reasons to (Alex, 2026-10-09)
parameters.alternative: bring the lowest flight band much closer to mountain height instead of (or as well as) raising the ground (Alex)

decisions.notes: Alex: 'I definitely think we will want some taller ground. Like I said, we should be mountainous islands to give some tactical options.' Later the same day: 'Let's leave mountains off for now. We'll come back and visit them once we have reasons to. Another way to do it would be having the lowest flight level be much closer to mountain height.'

decisions.question: What does the turn preview assume about enemies?
options: the player picks an enemy plan to simulate, the dumb plan by default
decisions.chosen: open

parameters.fixed: there will be a preview function; it must not reveal the enemies' real plans

decisions.status: open: Alex's design point, not decided
decisions.notes: Alex: 'This is actually an open design point. We almost certainly want to give the player a preview function, but we don't want them to know the plans of the enemies.'

decisions.question: How do players edit plans together?
options: live drafts in each player's colour, with who is editing a unit shown (proposed)
decisions.chosen: last edit wins, with a full preview

parameters.rule: any player can edit any unit; the last edit stands
parameters.visibility: every player sees every unit's plan live, and which units have plans and which do not

applied_to: nothing yet: the first-fight pass builds it (proposed plan in the design doc)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Last edit wins with full preview so you can see what has plans and what doesn't.'

decisions.question: Who resolves a turn in a networked game?
options: the host resolves and sends the result (proposed)
every peer resolves from the shared plans (lockstep)
decisions.chosen: the host

parameters.rule: the host plays out the turn and sends every player the result; peers play back what the host sends

applied_to: nothing yet: the first-fight pass builds it (proposed plan in the design doc)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Host'.

decisions.question: What happens to a plane that goes down?
options: it stops where it went down (the first brief's placeholder)
it explodes mid-air, or goes out of control and crashes eventually
decisions.chosen: it explodes mid-air, or the players lose control of it and it crashes eventually

parameters.proposed_details: the fate is a seeded roll at the moment it goes down; out of control = nobody can plan it, the sim flies it down in a spiral over one or more turns until it hits the ground (a crash event); the chance and the fall are proposed values in data/sim/combat.json

applied_to: Track C (combat), Track X (effects board), Track U2 (roster), in progress
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Dead planes should either explode mid air or lose control by players and crash eventually.'

decisions.question: If another player edits a plan after I am Ready, is my Ready withdrawn?
options: only the editor's own Ready is withdrawn
decisions.chosen: other players' edits do not unready you

parameters.rule: an edit withdraws only the editing player's Ready

decisions.notes: Alex: 'Other player edits should not unready you.'

decisions.question: Does the roster get a filter or grouping for units that need orders?
decisions.chosen: a group-by for needs orders
decisions.notes: Alex: 'We want a group by for needs orders.'

decisions.question: Is the health arc on the selection ring drawn for enemy planes too?
decisions.chosen: own planes only, for now
decisions.notes: Alex: 'The health ring can stay on our planes for now.'

decisions.question: A player who joins mid-turn: must they Ready before the turn plays, or watch until the next turn?
options: the joiner is an unready player and holds the turn until they Ready
the joiner watches until the next turn
decisions.chosen: all players must ready up, joiners included

parameters.rule: a player who joins mid-turn holds the turn until they Ready

decisions.notes: Alex: 'All players must ready up.'

decisions.question: Track E's open questions: the bomber's starting band; evading by band change; an escort re-engaging after breaking off for health
options: evade by changing one band (costs speed) / weave only
an escort that broke off for health never re-engages / may re-engage
decisions.chosen: the bomber can start high; evading by a one-band change stays; an escort that broke off for health does not re-engage, for now

parameters.bomber_start_band: high (the players must climb to reach it)
parameters.evade: weave plus a change of one band (data/sim/ai.json strike.*)

decisions.notes: Alex: '1. Bomber can start high 2. Sounds good 3 fine for now' -- read as answers to Track E's three questions (the lead's reading).

decisions.question: A lone light fighter on a bomber's tail is shot down first about 45% of the time. Intended?
decisions.chosen: yes: grouping is the better tactic when the target outmasses you
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Yes, that means grouping is better tactic when target out masses you.'

decisions.question: Should hit odds depend on distance (a light fighter 420 m back outranges a 400 m tail turret every time)?
options: odds fall off with range now
decisions.chosen: guns fire slightly over their effective range: full odds inside it, falling off just past it

parameters.rule: a second odds factor, range: 1 inside the effective range, falling smoothly to 0 over a short overshoot past it (proposed size in data/sim/combat.json)

decisions.notes: Alex: 'Slightly over effective range.' (The lead's reading: odds fall off past the effective range rather than a hard cutoff.)

decisions.question: Should a crash do anything on the ground?
options: an explosion, then a smoking wreck
decisions.chosen: an explosion, then smoking
applied_to: Track X's crash board, in progress
decisions.notes: Alex: 'A explosion then smoking - show me the panel.'

decisions.question: With odds falling off past effective range, a light fighter about 470 m behind a bomber still wins 98% (wing guns effective to 450 m, the tail turret to 400 m). Match the ranges, or keep the gap?
options: match the tail turret's effective range to the wing guns
decisions.chosen: keep the gap: a reward for good positioning
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Reward'.

decisions.question: How do your own units stand out on the busy background?
decisions.chosen: A, today's marker -- none of the new options was quite there
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Board 1 - not quite there. Today's is the best.' The problem (e.g. the heavy fighter faint over trees) stays open for a later round. Alex's own idea for the next round (2026-10-10): 'For locating the players planes, what about wingtip trails in the players color? That cover the past turn.' Board in progress: variants/wingtip-trails/.

decisions.question: The proposed fire accent oklch(0.72 0.14 56), a light saturated orange, for flashes, fireballs, flames and embers

decisions.question: Wingtip trails in the players' colour covering the past turn (Alex's idea): which treatment?
options: C lines broken at each step
D one ribbon between the wingtips
E lines and a rung at each step
decisions.chosen: D, one ribbon between the wingtips

parameters.marker.trails.applies_to: all (every moving unit in sight, each in its side colour)

E closing ring and lit label

decisions.question: Should relative velocity affect hit odds?
decisions.chosen: yes: relative velocity has an accuracy impact

parameters.proposed_design: a third odds factor: the line of sight's crossing rate costs the most, closing speed less or nothing; fixed guns hurt more than flexible guns and turrets, whose gunners track (per-weapon tracking values in data)

decisions.notes: Alex: 'Relative velocity should also have an accuracy impact.' The second factor Alex has named after the cone's centre (hit-odds) and range (effective-range).

choose the step to drop on

a side-view indicator (Alex's harder idea, being described)

decisions.question: How does a special (the bomb today) get its target, and how is its area of effect shown?
decisions.board: none (options in chat: A aim on the step, B a target per step, C a target selection, D target first with the step found for you)
options: A aim on the step (as built)
D target first, the step found for you
decisions.chosen: a target selection: with a friendly unit selected, the player can also select an enemy unit or a point on the map as its target. The target does only two things: it shows on the side view, and it is what the unit's special uses when activated. Non-special weapons need no target: they fire on their own

parameters.target: an enemy unit or a point on the map, selected while a friendly unit is selected
effects: the target a special uses when activated

decisions.notes: Alex: 'For bombs, I expected area of effect as well. This implies each step might have a target which is either a unit or point. But this is only for specials. Let's look at our options here. Maybe a targeting selection is the right call. Specials use the current selection to set their target.' And: 'For selection, does this imply we have both a player unit and enemy unit selection?' Then: 'For targeting what I was actually thinking is when you have a friendly unit selected, you can also select either an enemy unit or a point on the map. The only thing it does is show on the side view and it is the target that the special will use if activated. Non-specials don't need targets because they autofire.' Still open (asked): how the target is set, whether each unit keeps its own, a drop whose target is outside the step's cone, no target set, the aim handle; and how the area of effect is drawn (a board).
